quiz on friday, covers wk4-6
reminder: lab report due 14/11 via moodle

Atkinson-Shiffrin model (1968) - multi-store model: sensory memory -> STM -> LTM
sensory memory lasts < 1 sec for visual (iconic), ~2-4 sec for auditory (echoic)
STM capacity 7 +/- 2 items (Miller, 1956), duration approx 18-30 sec w/o rehearsal
chunking = grouping info into meaningful units to increase STM capacity
LTM - basically unlimited capacity

Working memory model (Baddeley & Hitch 1974)
  - central executive: controls attention, coordinates the slave systems
  - phonological loop: holds verbal / auditory info (inner voice)
  - visuospatial sketchpad: visual + spatial info (inner eye)
  - episodic buffer (added 2000) - links info across domains

types of LTM:
explicit (declarative) vs implicit (non-declarative)
episodic memory - personal experiences, e.g. your 10th birthday
semantic memory - general facts / knowledge e.g. Paris is capital of France
procedural memory - skills, like riding a bike

serial position effect: better recall of items at start (primacy) and end (recency) of a list
proactive interference - old info disrupts new learning
retroactive interference - new info disrupts recall of old

HM (Henry Molaison) - bilateral medial temporal lobectomy 1953, couldnt form new explicit LTMs -> anterograde amnesia
